apps.name: Dispatcher
apps.description: Schedule outbound pickups and inbound arrivals, track load progress, and view daily timelines.
apps.releaseNotes:
Dispatcher 1.1.3

Swipe left or right on Inbounds and Outbounds to select the next or previous filter. A swipe must cover at least a quarter of the page width, with a 96 dp minimum, before switching on release. Short swipes, vertical scrolling, and search-field gestures do not switch filters. The Today page retains its existing timeline gestures.

Loading dots on Print and Start Loading buttons now draw as one compact indicator, preventing device fonts or display sizes from wrapping the dots onto another line.

Install over the existing app to retain saved settings and authorization. The package ID and signing certificate are unchanged.

apps.name: MES Radio
apps.description: Push-to-talk for your MES team. Talk on radio channels and replay received voice.
apps.releaseNotes:
MES Radio 1.0.7

Live speech gets progressively quieter when the speaker is estimated to be within 5 meters. At 5 meters or beyond, it uses your saved Quiet, Medium or Loud level. Live speech is reduced, not fully muted.
Recordings keep their original audio, and Replay plays at your saved listening level regardless of how close the speaker was.
Works for regular channels and Broadcast. A nearby-speaker status explains when live volume is lowered.

Both phones must enable location sharing and have fresh positions reporting accuracy of 5 meters or better. Missing, old or imprecise positions leave live volume unchanged. Location remains an estimate, and sharing stops when the app leaves the foreground; this does not guarantee feedback prevention. Two-phone proximity and acoustic testing remain pending.

Keeps the Broadcast speaker toggle, speech-reactive glow, radar stabilization and connection recovery from previous releases.
Android 9 or newer. Updates MES Radio in place and preserves sign-in, settings and voice history. Do not uninstall before updating.

apps.name: MES Run Beta
apps.description: Run production, coordinate MES staff, and follow line progress in an isolated test environment.
apps.releaseNotes:
MES Run Beta 12 - Machine Library and MES Parameters

The machine picker now includes Clamp Shell Suck Fill Machine, Pallet Hand Wrap and Pallet Machine Wrap, plus the revised Box Sealing Machine. Fiber Feeding Machine is the updated name for the yellow-conveyor figure. One Overlock Sewing option remains. All 19 figures can be selected independently for lines and production steps.

Machine profiles now follow the MES line configuration. Hayes has eight profiles with their configured descriptions and 19 settings each; Hai Jing currently has no configured profiles. Choose a profile explicitly when more than one is available. Production setup shows Line Speed and Fill Weight; Parameters shows the full settings. Each new run preserves its selected profile metadata, and changing running settings creates a new lot while retaining earlier history.

Update MES Run Beta in MES Store and use the existing test PIN. Try the new pictures in Swipe Line > Edit, then review profile selection and parameter details before starting a sample run. Employee references, attendance and product identities remain linked to MES. Production commands, quantities, raw materials and product fill weights remain isolated sample data. Pallet label printing belongs to a separate app.

Signed-release installation and installation through MES Store remain unverified because automatic approval review previously blocked those checks. Native checks use emulator debug builds. Physical printing, inspector submissions and live Andon inputs are outside this release.

apps.name: MES Store
apps.description: Your MES apps and updates, together in one place.
apps.releaseNotes:
MES Store 1.2.16

MES Store now checks for updates when you return to it, every five minutes while it stays open, and when the connection comes back while the store is open. A one-minute cooldown prevents repeated checks during quick app switches.

Background update checks now run approximately hourly instead of daily, subject to Android battery and network scheduling. Existing daily schedules are upgraded automatically.

Catalog checks can use any internet connection. The unmetered-only setting continues to apply to automatic APK downloads. Automatic checks still respect your setting, and Android still asks before installing updates.

Install over MES Store to preserve settings and downloads. Android 9 or newer; the package ID and release signing key are unchanged.
